title: Frontend: Memoization
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Memoization. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(calls). Memoize the numeric two-argument function (a,b)=>a*b+a with exact ordered argument keys. Return {outputs,evaluations}; repeated calls reuse even a zero result.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Choose keys that match the function’s semantics.
alternativeApproaches: Combine memoization with LRU capacity and document whether concurrent callers share a pending promise.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Falsey result; multiple arguments; object identity.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
